definition: Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, irrespective of the size of the molecules.
msAccepts: equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules
msAvoids: equal volumes contain equal numbers of atoms (for molecular gases)

definition: The conditions at which gas-volume calculations are quoted in this course: about 20-25 °C and 1 atmosphere pressure, abbreviated rtp.
msAccepts: rtp
room temperature and pressure (about 20-25 °C and 1 atm)

definition: The volume unit 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³ = 1 litre. Gas molar volumes and solution concentrations are both quoted per dm³; convert cm³ to dm³ by dividing by 1000.
msAccepts: 1 dm³ = 1000 cm³
1 dm³ is the same as 1 litre

definition: The volume occupied by 1 mole of any gas: 24 dm³ (24 000 cm³) at rtp. The same for every gas, because equal moles hold equal numbers of molecules.
msAccepts: 24 dm³ (or 24 000 cm³) per mole at rtp
volume of 1 mole of any gas at rtp
msAvoids: a volume that depends on which gas it is
24 dm³ at any temperature and pressure

definition: More than enough of a reactant to react with all of the other reactant; some is left over. 'Added to excess' means the other substance reacts completely.
msAccepts: more than enough to react with all of the other reactant
some left over after the reaction is complete
msAvoids: the reactant that runs out first

definition: The amount of substance dissolved per dm³ of solution, in mol/dm³; or the mass per dm³, in g/dm³. Convert between them with Mᵣ: divide g/dm³ by Mᵣ, multiply mol/dm³ by Mᵣ.
msAccepts: amount of solute per dm³ of solution
moles per cubic decimetre

definition: The symbol M for concentration in mol/dm³: '2 M' hydrochloric acid means 2 mol/dm³, read as '2 molar'.
msAccepts: M means mol/dm³
2 M = 2 mol/dm³

definition: A technique that measures exactly what volume of one solution reacts with a volume of another of known concentration, so an unknown concentration can be calculated.
msAccepts: finding the reacting volumes of two solutions
using a burette and pipette to find an unknown concentration

definition: The long graduated tube with a tap that runs one titration solution into the other, delivering a variable measured volume (read to 0.05 cm³).
msAccepts: delivers variable measured volumes of solution
run from it until the indicator changes colour
msAvoids: the flask the reaction happens in

definition: The calibrated tube that measures one accurate fixed volume of solution (e.g. 25.0 cm³ of alkali) into the conical flask before titrating.
msAccepts: measures a fixed volume accurately
transfers the alkali into the conical flask

definition: The point in a titration at which the indicator just changes colour — the reaction is just complete. Approached by running the burette solution in drop by drop.
msAccepts: when the indicator just changes colour
the reaction is just complete
msAvoids: when the colour changes permanently to pink for every indicator
